\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উদ্দেশ্য} (uddeshyô)}{উদ্দেশ্য (uddeshyô)}]{\bn{উদ্দেশ্য} (uddeshyô) — a purpose; an aim}

\label{lesson:BN-C331-uddeshyo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a reaction, then the Bengali for an inspiration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উদ্দেশ্য}}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্দেশ্য}} — \emph{uddeshyô} — \textquotedblleft{}a purpose; an aim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{মিটিংয়ের} \bn{উদ্দেশ্য} \bn{কী}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei miṭingyer uddeshyô kī?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
What is this meeting for?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্দেশ্য}} (\emph{uddeshyô}) is Sanskrit \emph{uddeśya}, the thing one points at or has in view (Monier-Williams). Bengali uses it for the purpose behind a plan or a meeting.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uddeshyô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uddeshyô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei miṭingyer uddeshyô kī?} — What is this meeting for?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a reaction, then the Bengali for an inspiration, then say \emph{uddeshyô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উদ্দেশ্য} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A purpose; an aim\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উপকার} (upôkār)}{উপকার (upôkār)}]{\bn{উপকার} (upôkār) — a benefit; a good turn}

\label{lesson:BN-C331-upokar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an inspiration, then the Bengali for a purpose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উপকার}}
\textbf{\bn{উপকার}} — \emph{upôkār} — \textquotedblleft{}a benefit; a good turn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তোমার} \bn{পরামর্শে} \bn{আমার} \bn{অনেক} \bn{উপকার} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tomār pôrāmôrshe āmār ônek upôkār hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Your advice did me a lot of good.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উপকার}} (\emph{upôkār}) is Sanskrit \emph{upakāra}, help or a favour done (Monier-Williams). With \bn{হওয়া} the benefit happens to someone: \bn{আমার} \bn{উপকার} \bn{হল}, it did me good.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upôkār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upôkār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tomār pôrāmôrshe āmār ônek upôkār hôlô.} — Your advice did me a lot of good.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an inspiration, then the Bengali for a purpose, then say \emph{upôkār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উপকার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A benefit; a good turn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{লাভ} (lābh)}{লাভ (lābh)}]{\bn{লাভ} (lābh) — a gain; a profit}

\label{lesson:BN-C331-labh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a purpose, then the Bengali for a good turn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{লাভ}}
\textbf{\bn{লাভ}} — \emph{lābh} — \textquotedblleft{}a gain; a profit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{ব্যবসায়} \bn{কি} \bn{কোনো} \bn{লাভ} \bn{আছে}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei bæbsāy ki kono lābh āchhe?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Is there any profit in this business?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{লাভ}} (\emph{lābh}) is Sanskrit \emph{lābha}, getting or gaining (Monier-Williams). It covers money made in trade and any advantage gained.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lābh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lābh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei bæbsāy ki kono lābh āchhe?} — Is there any profit in this business?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a purpose, then the Bengali for a good turn, then say \emph{lābh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{লাভ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A gain; a profit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{লোকসান} (loksān)}{লোকসান (loksān)}]{\bn{লোকসান} (loksān) — a financial loss}

\label{lesson:BN-C331-loksan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a good turn, then the Bengali for a profit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{লোকসান}}
\textbf{\bn{লোকসান}} — \emph{loksān} — \textquotedblleft{}a financial loss\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গত} \bn{বছর} \bn{দোকানটার} \bn{লোকসান} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gôtô bôchhôr dokānṭār loksān hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shop made a loss last year.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{লোকসান}} (\emph{loksān}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{nuqṣān}, a shortfall, which would have come into Bengali through Persian, with the first n heard as l. It is the opposite of \bn{লাভ} in trade.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{loksān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{loksān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gôtô bôchhôr dokānṭār loksān hôlô.} — The shop made a loss last year.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a good turn, then the Bengali for a profit, then say \emph{loksān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{লোকসান} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A financial loss\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উপযোগী} (upôjogī)}{উপযোগী (upôjogī)}]{\bn{উপযোগী} (upôjogī) — useful; serviceable}

\label{lesson:BN-C331-upojogi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a profit, then the Bengali for a financial loss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উপযোগী}}
\textbf{\bn{উপযোগী}} — \emph{upôjogī} — \textquotedblleft{}useful; serviceable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{বইটা} \bn{ছাত্রদের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{উপযোগী।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei bôiṭā chhātrôder jônyô upôjogī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This book is useful for students.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উপযোগী}} (\emph{upôjogī}) is Sanskrit \emph{upayogin}, serving a use (Monier-Williams), from \emph{upayoga}, use. What it is useful for takes -\bn{এর} \bn{জন্য}: \bn{ছাত্রদের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{উপযোগী}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upôjogī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upôjogī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei bôiṭā chhātrôder jônyô upôjogī.} — This book is useful for students.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a profit, then the Bengali for a financial loss, then say \emph{upôjogī} again
\end{itemize}
